transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-20
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Leah Nguyen (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Eng Ops), Maya Thompson (Nexa Head of ML), Eric Zhao (Nexa Infra), Priya Kapoor (Nexa Security), Liam O'Connor (Nexa Data)

Optional Auto-summary: Quick recap of INT8/FP8 runs, perf numbers, and action items (see below)

[00:00:00] Samir: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call and then we'll jump into the numbers.
[00:00:10] Maya: hey hi, Maya here.
[00:00:15] Eric: Eric on infra.
[00:00:18] Priya: Priya, sec.
[00:00:20] Leah: Leah from Redwood, SE.
[00:00:24] Jordan: Jordan here.
[00:00:30] Samir: cool, so agenda — Leah will run through the INT8/FP8 results, then we discuss calibration and on-prem validation, and close with next steps.
[00:00:45] Leah: alright jumping in — so last week we ran the v2 quantized set: INT8 symmetric per-channel with per-layer calibration and FP8 block quant. We did both hosted and a simulated on-prem run on a 80GB A100 shape (emulated).
[00:01:10] Leah: top-line: INT8 reduced model memory by about 2.3x on average, FP8 was about 2.5x; latency per token increased slightly in the INT8 case for long sequences due to dequant/dequant overhead but on small prompt it's neutral. Throughput improved for batched workloads by ~1.8x for INT8 and ~2.0x for FP8 in our tests.
[00:01:45] Liam: when you say latency per token increased, can you quantify? we care about tail latency for clinical triage flows.
[00:01:53] Leah: yes so median latency stayed within SLO — around 120ms for 256-token prompt on hosted baseline fp16, INT8 median was 140ms, FP8 median 130ms. P95 saw a bit more variance — INT8 P95 hit 330ms in one run vs fp16 290ms. Could be batching and memory pressure plus dequant jitter.
[00:02:20] Maya: those deltas are ok but the P95 bump worries me. Our SLAs are 300ms for triage.
[00:02:26] Samir: understood — that's why Leah's follow-ups include stratified calibration and tuning the execution kernels. We can also switch routing policy during peak traffic to fallback to fp16 for sensitive routes.
[00:02:40] Priya: also from security side, the FP8/INT8 artifacts — do you have any additional risks for leakages or side-channels? we need to review with infra team.
[00:02:50] Leah: good question — quantization per se doesn't relax encryption in-memory; but on certain hardware you may need to ensure kernel-level protections and encrypted RAM if required. we'll provide a checklist for KMS/HSM and in-memory protections.
[00:03:10] Jordan: one note — in our simulated on-prem we used continuous batching with a small KV cache warm-up. The cache hit rate affects the perf deltas quite a bit. If Nexa's real workload has high prefix reuse, INT8 perf looks better.
[00:03:30] Eric: our workload does have a lot of prefix reuse for patient histories. what's the best way to capture that in the calibration?
[00:03:36] Leah: include representative prefix windows in the calibration set — we suggested adding 30-40% clinical notes and 20% short prompts, we saw calibration skew when calibration was mostly short prompts.
[00:03:55] Liam: i noticed in the example outputs some hallucination differences between fp16 and int8 on rare entity extraction — is that expected?
[00:04:02] Leah: yes small quality regressions on edge-case NER and numeric extraction were observed. overall generation quality measured by BLEU/Exact match was within 1-2% for most tasks but certain diagnostic prompts fell off by 4-6% with INT8. FP8 was closer to fp16 but had more variance depending on quant block boundaries.
[00:04:25] Maya: can you show a specific example?
[00:04:29] Leah: sure pulling up slide 6 — the numeric case where fp16 gives "BP 120/80" and INT8 outputs "approx 120" — small but clinically relevant. We can tune calibration and per-layer fallback to avoid quantizing the final LM head for certain models.
[00:04:52] Samir: just to clarify, per-layer fallback is a supported option in Redwood Optimize config and we can recommend a safe profile for triage.
[00:05:00] Maya: good. what's the plan for final validation? we need an on-prem run against our subset with encryption and realistic infra.
[00:05:07] Samir: propose we do an on-prem benchmark next month — Eric can provide a cluster window and dataset slice, Redwood runs the quantized model with our runtime in Nexa's env. Leah, Jordan to lead.
[00:05:18] Eric: that's fine. we're aiming for a two-hour window but can extend if needed.
[00:05:22] Leah: noted. for the next runs I'll add stratified calibration (more clinical notes), drop quant on the LM head and run INT8 again, and also test FP8 with different block sizes.
[00:05:36] Liam: what's your recommended block size for FP8?
[00:05:39] Leah: we tried 8 and 16; block size 8 reduced variance at the cost of a tiny perf hit. we can pick 8 for stability.
[00:05:50] Maya: ok. on security — Priya, any immediate blockers?
[00:05:54] Priya: we need docs on key management, audit logs, and data residency. also encryption at rest for the telemetry buckets. Redwood, can you share the SOC2 packet and the KMS integration guide?
[00:06:06] Samir: yes, we'll share SOC2 artifacts and a KMS/HSM checklist. we'll also include recommended RBAC roles for the private control plane.
[00:06:15] Priya: thanks, that helps.
[00:06:18] [00:06:20] Leah: quick perf note — in the hosted runs we tested with 4-thread kernel scheduling; on Nexa hardware you might see different perf with 2 sockets. We'll include a perf sensitivity matrix.
[00:06:36] Jordan: also logs — can we capture trace-level token latency and memory maps during the on-prem run? that will help root cause P95 spikes.
[00:06:45] Leah: yes, Redwood runtime supports token-level traces; we'll collect them but need permission to transfer logs (Priya).
[00:06:55] Priya: fine as long as sensitive PHI is redacted and transfer uses encrypted buckets.
[00:07:02] Samir: ok we'll add redaction guidance to the run playbook.
[00:07:08] [00:07:20] Eric: curious on cost — do you have estimated cost delta for INT8/FP8 on hosted vs dedicated?
[00:07:27] Samir: approximate — INT8 reduces GPU-hour cost by ~30-40% due to increased packing and lower memory egress; FP8 similar but depends on kernel efficiency. For Dedicated reserved pools we can give a firm quote; Samir will send pricing options.
[00:07:46] Maya: we may prefer Dedicated if performance stability is critical. need to weigh cost vs risk.
[00:07:51] Samir: understood. We'll include a decision doc in the spreadsheet.
[00:07:58] [00:08:10] Leah: back to quality — for evaluation we ran a stratified eval set: clinical Q/A, NER, summarization. Overall ROUGE/BLEU delta small, but NER exact match dropped 4.5% with INT8. For FP8 it was 1.2% drop but variance up to 3% across runs.
[00:08:33] Liam: what about calibration drift over time? if model sees new vocab in production will calibration degrade?
[00:08:39] Leah: calibration is mostly about weight distributions; drift can matter if new tokens change activations significantly. For that we recommend periodical recalibration (weekly) or online calibration with a small sample. Redwood Optimize can automate suggestions.
[00:08:56] Maya: does Redwood support canary rollouts by partition so we can keep a small pct on fp16 for safety?
[00:09:02] Jordan: yes Redwood Console supports per-route rollouts and automatic fallback if quality metrics breach thresholds.
[00:09:10] Priya: perfect.
[00:09:12] [00:09:30] Samir: any other questions from Nexa?
[00:09:34] Maya: one more — training/finetune compatibility with quantized models? we plan small fine-tunes in house.
[00:09:40] Leah: quantized models are inference-only; fine-tuning needs fp16/fp32. You can do delta tuning then quantize. We'll doc a recommended workflow.
[00:09:50] Eric: ok.
[00:09:55] [00:10:10] Leah: quick demo of a sample output differences (apologies if transcription munges exact tokens):
[00:10:18] Leah: FP16: "Patient shows BP 120/80, recommend follow-up in 6 months."
[00:10:24] Leah: INT8: "Patient shows approx 120, recommend follow up" (missing diastolic)
[00:10:32] Leah: FP8: "Patient shows BP 120/80, recommend-followup in 6 months." (but sometimes drops punctuation)
[00:10:40] Maya: that's the kind of thing we can't miss.
[00:10:44] Samir: agreed — for clinical fields we'll recommend per-layer preservation for the head and stricter calibration.
[00:10:53] [00:11:05] Leah: adding to the benchmark spreadsheet: raw logs, token-level traces, calibration configs, and eval set buckets. Samir will share link.
[00:11:14] Samir: I'll share the sheet after this call.
[00:11:18] Priya: on compliance, please also share data retention policy for logs — default retention is 30 days?
[00:11:25] Samir: default hosted retention 30d but can be extended for Dedicated/Private. We'll include options.
[00:11:34] [00:11:50] Maya: timeline question — we want POC decision by end of November. Is that feasible?
[00:11:56] Samir: yes, with on-prem run in early November and a final quality report mid-November that seems reachable.
[00:12:03] Leah: timeline action: run INT8 w/ stratified calibration by 10/27, FP8 block8 stability runs by 10/27, on-prem schedule for week of 11/02.
[00:12:15] [00:12:40] Jordan: one small ops note — if you go Dedicated, we recommend reserved instances with burst capacity to handle peaks so you don't see P95 spikes.
[00:12:48] Eric: noted.
[00:12:51] [00:13:10] Maya: any known gotchas around tokenizer differences post-quant?
[00:13:15] Leah: tokenizer is unchanged; issues show up as distributional shift in activations not tokenization. But we saw some end-of-sequence handling differences due to softmax quant rounding; we'll include mitigations.
[00:13:30] [00:13:50] Samir: ok let's do a quick recap of action items and next steps.
[00:13:55] Samir: Leah to rerun INT8 with stratified calibration and per-layer head preservation — due 10/27.
[00:14:02] Samir: Samir to send pricing and SOC2 + KMS docs by 10/22.
[00:14:07] Samir: Eric to provide dataset slice and cluster window by 10/26.
[00:14:12] Samir: Priya to confirm any redaction requirements for logs and accept encrypted transfer — by 10/23.
[00:14:18] Leah: we'll also add the perf sensitivity matrix and token-level traces to the shared sheet.
[00:14:24] Maya: thanks all.
[00:14:27] [00:14:40] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in thread.
[00:14:42] Meeting End

Notes/Links referenced: Benchmark spreadsheet link (shared post-call), SOC2 packet (shared via s3 link), Redwood Optimize profile examples, on-prem run playbook. Some transcript words may be munged by auto-transcription.
